---
title: "Greenland and Antarctic ice-sheet maps"
---

Interactive maps and A0 posters of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets:
surface ice velocity over hillshaded topography, with drainage regions, surface
contours, the median sea-ice edge, key numbers and place names. They are made
with Julia and CairoMakie; the code is on
[GitHub](https://github.com/fesmc/cryosphere-maps), and
[Data & methods](about.qmd) lists the sources and how the maps are made.

## Interactive maps

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Greenland →](greenland.qmd)
Ice velocity, surface and bed elevation at 500 m, with drainage regions,
contours, sea-ice edges and all glacier names (GeoNames). Search for a name to
find it.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Antarctica →](antarctica.qmd)
The same at 1 km, with drainage basins, the grounding line and the glaciers,
ice streams, ice shelves and domes of the SCAR Composite Gazetteer.
:::
:::

## Key numbers compared with published estimates

The key numbers on the posters are computed from BedMachine on the poster grids
(see [Data & methods](about.qmd)). They agree with published estimates within
the spread between datasets.

**Greenland** (BedMachine v6, 500 m grid)

| | Poster | Published |
|---|---|---|
| Ice volume | 2.98 × 10⁶ km³ | 2.99 ± 0.02 × 10⁶ km³ (BedMachine v3[^bm3]) |
| Sea-level equivalent | 7.4 m | 7.42 ± 0.05 m (BedMachine v3[^bm3]) |
| Ice area | 1.73 × 10⁶ km² | ~1.7 × 10⁶ km² (depends on what counts as peripheral ice) |
| Maximum thickness | 3411 m | ~3.4 km |

**Antarctica** (BedMachine v4, 1 km grid), compared with Table 5 of Bedmap3[^bm3a]

| | Poster | Bedmap2 | BedMachine v3 | Bedmap3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Area incl. ice shelves (10⁶ km²) | 13.85 | 13.92 | 13.59 | 13.63 |
| Grounded area (10⁶ km²) | 12.30 | 12.30 | 12.35 | 12.10 |
| Volume incl. ice shelves (10⁶ km³) | 26.92 | 26.92 | 26.77 | 27.17 |
| Sea-level equivalent (m) | 58.1 | 58 | 58 | 58 |
| Maximum thickness (m) | 5015 | 4897 | 4822 | 4757 |

- The regional sea-level equivalents (East 52.4 m, West 5.4 m, Peninsula
  0.35 m) add up to the total and agree with the 52 m (East) and 5 m (West) of
  Bedmap1[^bm1].
- The ice-shelf area (1.55 × 10⁶ km²) is close to Bedmap2 (1.62) and Bedmap3
  (1.53).
- The maximum thickness is the least robust number: it depends on the bed
  product. On the poster it lies in the Denman Glacier trough (67.5°S,
  99.3°E), the deepest bed in BedMachine; Bedmap3 puts its thickest ice at
  76°S, 118°E.
- BedMachine thicknesses are ice-equivalent (firn air removed), so volume and
  sea-level equivalent need no firn correction.

[^bm3]: Morlighem et al. (2017), BedMachine v3, *Geophys. Res. Lett.* 44, doi:[10.1002/2017GL074954](https://doi.org/10.1002/2017GL074954).
[^bm3a]: Pritchard et al. (2025), Bedmap3, *Scientific Data* 12, 414, doi:[10.1038/s41597-025-04672-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04672-y).
[^bm1]: Lythe et al. (2001), BEDMAP, *J. Geophys. Res.* 106, 11335–11351, doi:[10.1029/2000JB900449](https://doi.org/10.1029/2000JB900449).
